stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rain and power cuts dampen spirit of Deepavali
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rain and power cuts dampen spirit of Deepavali
stories.summary: Heavy downpour and power cuts have dampened the festival spirit among everyone, right from kids to elderly people and farmers to retail vendors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu has played spoilsport on Deepavali celebrations across SPSR Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram districts, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Heavy downpour and power cuts have dampened the festival spirit among everyone, right from kids to elderly people and farmers to retail vendors.
Generally, households purchase crackers and diyas (earthenware lamps) on Deepavali morning or a day ahead.
Due to continuous rains during the last couple of days, many of them remained indoors and those, who came out, unable to find the good quality products.
Madan Mohan, an intermediate student from Dhanalakshmipuram in Nellore, said, “The rains have disrupted our plans of fireworks this year.
Neither we could buy crackers, nor play with whatever we had kept aside last year.”
The situation was much horrible in Prakasam district.
The people faced problems in commuting because of the inundated roads.
The elderly persons couldn’t come out of their homes for medicines and other basic needs.
The power cuts led to mosquito menace at homes.
As the heavy rains lashed several parts of the district, the electricity lines, poles, conductors and distribution transformers have extensively damaged.
Despite of the swift restoration works in progress, the power supply was not yet rectified in the rural areas by Monday (November 9, 2026) evening.

stories.headline: Pest Outbreak Strikes Flood Ravaged Paddy Fields Across Upper Assam Districts
stories.title: Pest Outbreak Strikes Flood Ravaged Paddy Fields Across Upper Assam Districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: A severe agricultural crisis is gripping Upper Assam as a massive infestation of swarming caterpillars sweeps through areas already devastated by monsoon floods.

Agriculture experts, on Tuesday, have identified Kamal Chapori, Bamunpukhuri, No. 1 Chintamoni Garh, and Nepali Khuti in Sivasagar district, alongside Disang Pani in Charaideo district, among the worst-affected pockets.
Field reports indicate that several other remote locations have sustained severe crop damage but are yet to be formally documented by the authorities.
The 2026 Assam floods left Sivasagar and Charaideo reeling from widespread destruction.
However, as the floodwaters from the Dikhow and Disang rivers receded, they left behind optimal breeding conditions for pests.
The infestation has quickly spread across nearly 2,400 hectares of paddy fields.
Charaideo has been hit the hardest, with approximately 1,600 hectares compromised, while Sivasagar has seen over 750 hectares of crops ravaged weeks before entering their crucial flowering phase.
“Swarming caterpillars can destroy paddy crops in vast areas overnight," warned Rizvi Hazarika, District Agriculture Officer (in charge) for Charaideo.
"This year, the attack has been particularly severe because the flood carried bigger numbers of caterpillars into the paddy fields.”
For local farmers, the pest onslaught is a secondary blow after losing assets and livestock to the sudden summer deluge.
Many areas, like Nepali Khuti, were entirely unprepared for the sheer volume of water that hit them in July.
"When the floods came rushing, everything washed away in a matter of hours," shared a resident.

stories.headline: Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall Street
stories.title: Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall Street
stories.summary: As the frenzy around artificial intelligence (AI) fizzles out, Morgan Stanley has struck a positive note, with the international brokerage firm seeing buying opportunities among AI enablers, infrastructure providers and adopters.After Democratic victories in the US midterm elections triggered concerns that a Democrat-controlled Congress would curb excessive AI spending on data centres, tech stocks plunged and have been trading on a seesaw since then. Morgan Stanley noted that Wall Street had undergone an earthquake event over the past week, with significant uncertainty surrounding the impact of the midterms on the data centre build-out, the trajectory of the cycle and the implications for global stocks.It broadly views the recent market weakness as unwarranted. “We see the market moves as an overreaction and think the ultimate impact will be a push-out of some projects from 2028 to 2029, rather than a derailing of the capex story. This has the potential to elongate the AI capex cycle, which has positives including a smoother supply-demand rebalancing across the data centre supply chain, improved credit outlook, and higher lease rates for compute,” it said.Also read | Anthropic retracts details of $69 billion IPO filing sent to bankers. Why analysts are raising worries over valuationsMorgan Stanley has sized the impact on the data centre build-out and flagged implications for stocks, policy and equity strategy across the US, Asia and Europe. "We are recommending a selective ‘Buy the Drop’ strategy and remain most constructive on the hyperscalers, select semis/infrastructure/time-to-power solutions that have de-rated materially, and software enablers and AI adopters as AI value creation broadens,” it further said.How Trump's midterm defeat can impact the AI tradeThe newly elected Democratic governors are unlikely to disrupt projects under construction, leaving 2027 projects unchanged, Morgan Stanley said. However, it believes some 2028 projects in Texas and Ohio will be delayed to 2029, as governors work with legislators to put in place new requirements for data centre developers.The international research firm shifted 5 GW of US data centre capacity from 2028 to 2029, representing 20% of US projects and 10% of global projects. This implies that US data centre capacity additions will decline 4% year-on-year in 2028 and rise 38% year-on-year in 2029. Globally, this implies data centre additions will rise 9% year-on-year in 2028 and 20% in 2029.“This could create an air-pocket across the tech supply chain in 2028, leading to a reduction in pricing power or a build of inventory, although we believe valuations are pricing this in across many names, with the key risk being the sustainability of margins. We also believe this creates an attractive opportunity to potentially build data centres abroad and forecast 20GW of potential spillover across Asia and EMEA,” it added.That said, Morgan Stanley is mindful that delays in project approvals or initiation, on top of existing constraints around labour and materials, could put downward pressure on its 2028 capex estimates and prolong the build-out and capex cycle.“We are highly focused on increased (exponential) compute efficiencies from leading labs in 2027 to allow products to scale with less compute. Compute constraints aren't new, and they may just stay around longer with further data centre delays,” it added.Finally, financing remains available, but the midterms should deepen the quality divide, Morgan Stanley said. With capex forecasts unchanged, it still expects higher AI-related debt issuance in 2027, led by hyperscalers. New construction financings and neoclouds face greater scrutiny, making tenant quality, a credible path to energisation and contractual protections increasingly important.“We see more limited exposure to new restrictions for projects already backing outstanding bonds, although execution risk remains. Slower competing development should support stabilised, cash-flowing assets, reinforcing our preference for colocation over hyperscaler data-centre ABS.”Also read | Nithin Kamath says speculative craziness brought more people into US markets: ‘Nothing expands markets like greed, FOMO’Which AI stocks to buy?Given the significant price weakness across a range of AI-related stocks following the US election results, Morgan Stanley provided its updated views on which stocks or sectors look most attractive, highlighting three key areas. It has three main buckets of investment recommendations.These include hyperscalers (Amazon, Meta, Google and Microsoft), select data centre supply chain names, and software enablers or AI adopters. Nvidia is also mentioned among the stocks, but it belongs to the semiconductor category rather than the hyperscaler category. The brokerage also suggested a ‘Buy the Drop’ approach, identifying selective ways to play the AI investment opportunity post-midterms.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. stories.headline: India remains key drug supplier to US amid push for self-reliance
stories.title: India remains key drug supplier to US amid push for self-reliance
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 10 : India's vast pharmaceutical manufacturing network has emerged as a critical pillar of the US healthcare system, highlighting the challenges facing American President Donald Trump's efforts to bring generic drug production back to the United States, according to a report. A report by The Star highlighted a manufacturing facility operated by a leading pharmaceuticals firm in Hyderabad, nearly 1,900 workers produce more than 100 generic medicines, ranging from cholesterol and allergy treatments to antidepressants. The plant manufactures close to one billion oral doses every month with roughly three-quarters of output destined for the US market, it added. The scale of India's generic drug industry has made the country indispensable to global medicine supplies. Generic medicines account for about 90 per cent of prescriptions dispensed in the United States, while Indian manufacturers supply around 40 per cent of those medicines. Trump has proposed steep tariffs on imported generic drugs, including a 100 per cent levy from 2028 and a 200 per cent tariff a year later as part of a broader push to expand domestic manufacturing. However, industry executives and healthcare experts said that cost advantages built over decades make large-scale reshoring difficult, according to the report. According to industry estimates, producing most generic medicines in the United States could cost four times more than manufacturing them in India. Lower labour costs, faster factory construction timelines and extensive technical expertise continue to give Indian drugmakers a competitive edge. The industry's rise dates back to the 1970s, when India prioritised affordable access to medicines and developed strong capabilities in reverse-engineering and manufacturing pharmaceutical products at scale. While concerns over manufacturing quality once clouded the industry's reputation, leading drugmakers say regulatory oversight has strengthened significantly. Major producers now face frequent inspections by global regulators and have invested heavily in compliance systems. Industry leaders argue that rather than decoupling, the United States and India should deepen cooperation, particularly as both countries seek to reduce dependence on China for pharmaceutical ingredients and strengthen supply-chain resilience, according to The Star. --IANS

stories.headline: SC asks WhatsApp, others to list measures to prevent digital arrest, related cyber crimes
stories.title: SC asks WhatsApp, others to list measures to prevent digital arrest, related cyber crimes
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 10: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country. In an order uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on October 29 in a suo motu case titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and like intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre). The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on November 23. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken. He had said the platform was working on a software to identify suspicious accounts and warn users. “WhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,” the bench said in its order. The top court, on October 29, had said financial institutions must be held accountable for digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds, emphasising that banks should be required to compensate victims for losses suffered where an investigation establishes that the fraud occurred due to the institution's failure to exercise due diligence. “We reiterate and emphasize that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must mandate and incorporate suitable provisions that require financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds and pay suitable compensation not less than the amount lost by the customer, where it is established that the fraud or crime occurred due to the failure on the part of the financial institution to exercise due diligence in preventing or reporting the act/incident,” the bench said in the order. During the hearing, the CJI had questioned why banks could not intervene when customers suddenly attempted to transfer unusually large sums of money that were inconsistent with their established transaction patterns. “We have also emphasised in the past various preventive safeguards that must be mandated for every financial institution. These may include temporarily suspending unusual or suspicious transactions inconsistent with the account's past transaction history, automatically intimating such transactions to the nearest police station, and subsequently physically verifying the reported transactions to ascertain their genuineness,” the order said. In order to ensure effective implementation of the regulatory measures proposed by the RBI, as well as the directions issued, the bench further directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions before this court on the next date of hearing. Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, the bench had said the proposed RBI regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability. The CJI had said the bench would first examine the proposed RBI Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, before permitting the regulatory process to proceed. The directions are proposed to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31. Describing banks as a "protective umbrella" for vulnerable customers, the CJI had said financial institutions possess information about their account holders, including their transaction histories, and should use that knowledge to prevent fraud before money leaves an account. Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the bench that substantial work had been undertaken to improve the detection of suspicious transactions and strengthen preventive mechanisms within the banking system. The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them. The agencies have also been asked to provide suggestions for the prevention, detection and prosecution of such offences. The DGPs of all states and Union territories have been directed to ensure compliance. The reports must be submitted to the inter-departmental committee coordinating the government's response, with reports furnished to the court also being forwarded to the committee, the bench directed.

These may include temporarily suspending unusual or suspicious transactions inconsistent with the account's past transaction history, automatically intimating such transactions to the nearest police station, and subsequently physically verifying the reported transactions to ascertain their genuineness,” the order said.

In order to ensure effective implementation of the regulatory measures proposed by the RBI, as well as the directions issued, the bench further directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions before this court on the next date of hearing.

Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, the bench had said the proposed RBI regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability.
The CJI had said the bench would first examine the proposed RBI Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, before permitting the regulatory process to proceed.
The directions are proposed to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31.

Describing banks as a "protective umbrella" for vulnerable customers, the CJI had said financial institutions possess information about their account holders, including their transaction histories, and should use that knowledge to prevent fraud before money leaves an account.

Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the bench that substantial work had been undertaken to improve the detection of suspicious transactions and strengthen preventive mechanisms within the banking system.

The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them.
The agencies have also been asked to provide suggestions for the prevention, detection and prosecution of such offences.
The DGPs of all states and Union territories have been directed to ensure compliance.

The reports must be submitted to the inter-departmental committee coordinating the government's response, with reports furnished to the court also being forwarded to the committee, the bench directed.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently directed the State of Uttar Pradesh to carry out an exercise identifying all undertrial prisoners in 55 districts who have been granted bail but have not been released due to failure to comply with bail conditions, including execution of sureties.

The Court has stated that the exercise would cover all undertrial prisoners irrespective of whether they have engaged a private lawyer or have sought assistance of the District Legal Services Authority(DLSA).
Further, it must be carried out with the help of the concerned DLSA.

A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale passed these directions in a suo motu matter in which the issue related to the release of undertrials who haven't been released due to their unwillingness or inability to furnish bail sureties.
The bench made clear that this can't be an adversarial litigation where benefit is only extended to those who are being given assistance of NALSA.
"This direction shall be applicable even to those under-trial prisoners who could not comply with the bail conditions, despite the fact that they have engaged the private lawyers.
There cannot be any differentiation between the under-trial prisoners, who have the assistance of District Legal Services Authority and those who have engaged private counsel."
The orders were passed after hearing the submissions made by the Senior Advocate for the State of Uttar Pradesh, Pradeep Mishra, counsel for NALSA and the petitioners.
It was informed to the Court that in UP, there are 264 undertrial prisoners who have been granted bail, out of which only 158 have been released.
106 prisoners are yet to be released due to the want of execution of sureties, or other conditions imposed by the Trial Court.
It was further informed that the 264 prisoner statistic is only for 20 districts.
NALSA is yet to carry out such exercise of identifying undertrials in 55 districts.

stories.headline: Odisha Cabinet Approves Rs. 4,708-Cr, 600 MW Upper Indravati PSP Project
stories.title: Odisha Cabinet Approves Rs. 4,708-Cr, 600 MW Upper Indravati PSP Project
stories.summary: The Odisha government has approved a proposal to develop the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project (PSP) at Ranibahal in Kalahandi district. The PSP project is expected to be constructed with ₹4,708.64 crore estimated investment. The project aims to strengthen the state's energy storage capacity and improve grid stability. Currently, several entities are pursuing pumped storage development in Odisha. NHPC, for instance, has a pipeline of around 2,820 MW of PSP projects in the state. Meanwhile, the Odisha Renewable Energy Development Agency ( OREDA ) has partnered with NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL) to develop 525 MW of pumped storage projects, among other renewable energy projects. These pumped storage projects, along with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), can help manage the intermittency of renewable energy generation, improve grid stability and support the better integration of wind and solar power into the state's electricity network. The Odisha State Cabinet has also approved key amendments to the Odisha Pumped Storage Project ( PSP ) Policy, aimed at facilitating investments and providing greater flexibility to developers. The latest policy support is in addition to the incentives extended under the amendments to the Odisha Renewable Energy Policy (OREP), 2022. Under its revised 2026 policy, Odisha, for instance, provided an exemption of ₹0.20 per unit on State Transmission Utility (STU) charges for standalone BESS projects in the state. Incentives for Captive Projects Some of the benefits introduced through earlier amendments to Odisha's PSP Policy include changes to incentives for captive industries, with provisions allowing compliance through either renewable energy-based input energy or renewable energy consumed under the 'either-or' principle. Odisha's revised policy provides for a Right of First Refusal (RoFR) of up to 25% for captive users, while the limit for Independent Power Producers (IPPs) is set at up to 50%. The policy also provides for a state-level decision within 60 days, based on tariff viability.

Under its revised 2026 policy, Odisha, for instance, provided an exemption of ₹0.20 per unit on State Transmission Utility (STU) charges for standalone BESS projects in the state.

Some of the benefits introduced through earlier amendments to Odisha's PSP Policy include changes to incentives for captive industries, with provisions allowing compliance through either renewable energy-based input energy or renewable energy consumed under the 'either-or' principle.
Odisha's revised policy provides for a Right of First Refusal (RoFR) of up to 25% for captive users, while the limit for Independent Power Producers (IPPs) is set at up to 50%.
The policy also provides for a state-level decision within 60 days, based on tariff viability.

stories.headline: India's Shourya Ambure wins historic 100m hurdles bronze at Youth Olympics
stories.title: India's Shourya Ambure wins historic 100m hurdles bronze at Youth Olympics
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: DAKAR: Promising Indian sprinter Shourya Ambure won a historic bronze medal in the women’s 100m hurdles, clocking her personal best time at the Youth Olympics here.
Incidentally, the 17-year-old Ambure from Maharashtra was the only track and field athlete from India at the Games and she clocked a personal best time of 13.59 seconds to ensure a podium finish.
The gold was won by China’s Zhang Keyi with a wind assisted timing of 13.17 followed by Frenchwoman Anna Peeters, who clocked 13.57 seconds.
In fact, Ambure bettered her personal best twice on the same day, having clocked 13.77 seconds in the semifinal.
